note: The canonical rule catalogue for Hercules delivery documents. doc_lint.py is the only reader; the authoring skill summarises it and the commands echo its template. Edit a rule here, never in prose.

scenario_line.describes: One scenario per line: an identifier, a trigger, an arrow, and an observable outcome. A bullet that does not open with an identifier is ordinary prose, not a malformed scenario.

identifier_shape_note: Calibrated down from error to warning: an all-caps run matches business acronyms (SLA, GDPR, VAT) and a mixed-case run matches brand names a requirement may legitimately name (PayPal, GitHub). Only the unambiguous shapes above block.
suggestion_closing_sentence: These are suggestions from Product, not decisions. Design owns the technical choice.
normative_note: Bullet style strips the subject and the modality a sentence carries, which is the most ambiguous prose form per word. These sections restore both: every bullet names its subject and states its obligation.

sections.name: Goal
sections.mandate: The problem in the user's words, and the change wanted.

sections.name: Users
sections.mandate: Each actor, and how they cope today without this.

sections.name: Scope
sections.mandate: In scope and out of scope, as noun phrases. Out of scope is never empty.

sections.name: Flows
sections.mandate: Per flow: a story line, then main, negative and corner scenario lines.

sections.name: Constraints
sections.mandate: Business, time, regulatory and integration constraints.

sections.name: Success criteria
sections.mandate: Measurable, each carrying a number or a named standard.

sections.name: Risks & unknowns
sections.mandate: Future risks and open assumptions. Mitigation plans belong in the spec.

sections.name: Technical suggestions (non-binding)
sections.mandate: The only place technical vocabulary is legal, and only as a suggestion.

sections.name: Design references
sections.mandate: Links to visual artifacts. Links only, never inline content.

sections.name: Challenge
sections.mandate: The one prose slot: the requirement restated, and the single hardest thing.

sections.name: Scope
sections.mandate: What this spec delivers, and the service it belongs to.

sections.name: Affected code
sections.mandate: Existing classes, methods and modules this touches. Each named, or marked NEW.

sections.name: Decision record
sections.mandate: Decision, chosen, rejected and why, risk, mitigation, revisit-when.

sections.name: Structure & patterns
sections.mandate: Each pattern named, with why, and one real use case. Deviations carry a why.

sections.name: Naming contract
sections.mandate: Domain vocabulary, names rejected, and why rejected.

sections.name: Implementation
sections.mandate: Key technical decisions and the constraints the code-of-conduct binds.

sections.name: Rules — DO / DON'T
sections.mandate: Two columns, imperative, each row independently testable.

sections.name: Risks & mitigations
sections.mandate: Risk, the signal that it is happening, the mitigation, and who owns it at build.

sections.name: Test suite
sections.mandate: Unit, integration, API and end-to-end scenarios, plus what must never be mocked.

sections.name: Acceptance criteria
sections.mandate: Given / When / Then per deliverable, each bound to a scenario identifier.

sections.name: Known violations
sections.mandate: Architecture or dependency rules expected to fail at scaffold time.

sections.name: Deletion note
sections.mandate: How this spec retires once its feature is delivered in code.

rules.title: required section missing
rules.fix: add the section, or lower the tier if the depth is not warranted

rules.title: sections out of order
rules.fix: reorder to match the template from `doc_lint.py template`

rules.title: placeholder text
rules.fix: write the real content, or delete the section entirely — an empty section is omitted, never stubbed

rules.title: required section is empty
rules.fix: fill it, or delete it if nothing real belongs there

rules.title: heading deeper than the limit
rules.fix: promote the content to a section, or turn it into a table

rules.title: unknown section heading
rules.fix: rename it to a section the standard defines, or move the content under one

rules.title: prose in a bullet-only section
rules.fix: turn each sentence into a bullet, a table row, or move it to the prose section

rules.title: ambiguous phrase
rules.fix: replace with a number, a named standard, or a MUST / MAY ... WHEN clause

rules.title: bullet longer than the limit
rules.fix: split it, or promote the detail to a table

rules.title: implementation detail outside the suggestions section
rules.fix: move it under 'Technical suggestions (non-binding)', or say it in business language

rules.title: identifier-shaped word in a business document
rules.fix: if this names a class or a field, move it to the suggestions section; if it is a brand or an acronym, leave it

rules.title: bullet opens with a pronoun
rules.fix: name the subject the bullet is about

rules.title: technical mandate in a business document
rules.fix: state the outcome the business needs; the technical choice belongs to Design

rules.title: suggestions section is not hedged
rules.fix: hedge each bullet, and close the section with its fixed sentence

rules.title: normative bullet carries no modal
rules.fix: write MUST, MUST NOT, or MAY ... WHEN, so the obligation is unambiguous

rules.title: flow is missing a main or negative scenario
rules.fix: add the missing class, or mark the flow 'scenarios: n/a' with a reason

rules.title: malformed scenario line
rules.fix: write it as '- M1 | trigger -> observable outcome'

rules.title: negative scenarios outnumbered by main scenarios
rules.fix: add negative scenarios — the failure space is unexamined, not absent

rules.title: duplicate scenario identifier
rules.fix: give each scenario its own identifier; identifiers are never reused

rules.title: more scenarios than the tier allows
rules.fix: cut to the budget, or split the feature into two

rules.title: filename does not match the pattern
rules.fix: rename to the dated, kebab-case form the standard defines

rules.title: risk row carries no mitigation
rules.fix: state the mitigation, or move the row to the requirements as an accepted risk

rules.title: revisit-when is not observable
rules.fix: name a metric, a date, or an event — never 'if problems arise'

rules.title: vendor name in a port or interface
rules.fix: name the role, not the vendor; the vendor belongs in the adapter

rules.title: weak name carries no behaviour
rules.fix: rename so a reader with no context knows what it does, or justify it in the naming contract

rules.title: document is below the tier floor
rules.fix: go deeper — at this tier the document is expected to carry more than this

rules.title: document is over the tier hard cap
rules.fix: cut, or move evidence and enumerations into an appendix file

rules.title: document is over the tier soft cap
rules.fix: cut, or say why the extra length is earned

rules.title: section is hollow
rules.fix: give it a referent — an identifier, a path, a number, an endpoint — or delete the section

rules.title: section repeats its own heading and adds nothing
rules.fix: lead with the answer; the heading already said the topic
